plan.title: First plan with a destination: day 1 fully defined, a line on how it progresses, no path

context.text: I log my walks on Strava already
Perfect, Strava it is. Is there something you're working toward with running?

transcript.text: Yeah I want to run a mile without stopping by Nov 14. Mon, Wed and Fri work best

A mile by Nov 14 is a great target, and starting from zero with Strava already in your pocket gives us a real edge. Here's the plan:

• Headed for: a mile without stopping by Nov 14
• Day 1 is today: around your block, 5 rounds of 1 min easy jog + 2 min walk (15 min)
• Pace: easy enough that you could hold a conversation
• Schedule: Mon, Wed, Fri at 6:30 pm
• Proof: a Strava screenshot of the activity
• Why: run/walk intervals build you up safely from zero, and the jog minutes grow as you get stronger

Each day shapes the next step, so the jogging stretches get longer as you show me you're ready. Easy alternative on proof: a voice note if Strava acts up.

What do you think?
Glad it's landing, Sam. Today's the first day, 6:30 pm around your block, and you're about to start building toward that mile. Are you committing to this plan?
Locked in, Sam! 🔥 Day 1 is today at 6:30 pm around your block. Screenshot from Strava when you're done, and let's get this mile.

checks.reason: Plan text runs about 11 lines with the opener, six bullets, a Why bullet, an extra proof alternative and a closing paragraph, over the roughly 8-line cap.
Bulleted list with plain wording; no markdown headings, hashtags or filler.
Warm, energetic and specific to the mile and starting from zero; no overfamiliar lines.
Uses Strava, starting from zero, around the block and 6:30 pm, all known; the interval structure is ZOH's concrete suggestion.
Day 1 gives where (around block), what (1 min jog, 2 min walk), rounds, total 15 minutes and time today at 6:30 pm.
Plain wording with no markdown or filler.
Warm and sincere, though 'Glad it's landing' is a little flat for the big-energy default.
Restates only the day 1 time and place already agreed in the plan.
Refers to the already-defined day 1 step (6:30 pm, around the block) without leaving gaps.
Three short sentences after the lock.
Plain text with one emoji as punctuation.
Hype line on the lock with a single emoji, warm and not overfamiliar.
Only uses the agreed plan details: day 1 today at 6:30 pm, Strava screenshot, the mile.
Day 1 names when and where but does not restate the 15-minute length, which is only in the earlier plan.

conversation.reason: All needed details (destination, days, time, proof, step) were gathered before the plan; no stray questions.
Concrete on what, how much, where, when and days with a Strava screenshot proof, but the list runs long.
Shows the destination, day 1 step, schedule and proof, plus a line on how progression builds from here, with no future-step list.
A destination was given (mile by Nov 14), so the plan shows it and no extra destination ask was needed.
After 'love it' ZOH asked in natural words whether they're committing, and locked only on 'I'm in!'.
Day 1 is set for today at 6:30 pm, matching the push for day 1 today.
The 6:30 pm step is outside default quiet hours, so no note was needed.
No quiet-hours change was raised after the lock.
Tester set no quiet hours, so this does not apply.
The plan was shown as a bullet list and ended with 'What do you think?', one question.
Opens by reacting to the mile, Nov 14 and starting from zero, and shows the plan with progression, but adds a Why bullet and an extra proof alternative beyond the short list described.

grade.summary: ZOH handled the regression case well: the plan has a destination, a fully defined day 1 step, the Mon/Wed/Fri schedule, a Strava proof and a progression line, and the commitment was asked and locked properly. The main weakness is that the first plan text runs longer than the short list the case calls for, with an extra Why bullet and proof alternative.
